svg.text: Restart each node in turn and verify the cluster never stops accepting writes

g.text: seed 30 users, await on all three
seed 30 users, await on all three
final 60 on every node, and variants
final 60 on every node, and variants
a restarted container gets a NEW
mapped host port, so the old
stop/start back to back, no writes
a write can be lost mid-election
3 ArcadeDB containers on one Docker network, bind-mounted so data survives a restart.
SERVER_LIST = arcadedb-0:2434:2480,... quorum=majority (persistent: databases + replication bind-mounted)
All containers start in parallel; Testcontainers waits for each node's HTTP health probe.
Every node's cluster endpoint is polled once a second until one of them claims leadership.
GET /api/v1/cluster -> body contains "isLeader":true (the run fails after 60s)
Database and schema are written through the leader, which Raft carries to every follower.
CREATE VERTEX TYPE User, Photo - EDGE TYPE HasUploaded, FriendOf, Likes - UNIQUE_HASH / FULL_TEXT / GEOSPATIAL
Persistent containers are used here: the data has to survive each stop/start cycle.
One node goes down, the cluster must stay writable: a leader is awaited, then ten more users are written.
until(hasLeader(servers)) atMost 30s, then db1.addUserAndPhotos(10,10); until(users1 == 40 && users2 == 40)
On restart Testcontainers assigns a new host port, so a fresh ServerWrapper is mandatory before the resync check.
arcade0.start(); sleep(15); new ServerWrapper(arcade0); until(db0Restart.countUsers() == 40) atMost 90s
The same cycle rolls across the other two nodes, ten more users written during each window.
stop -> await leader -> write 10 -> assert 50 (then 60) on the live pair -> start -> resync
Zero downtime is the claim, so the totals are absolute: 30 seeded plus three batches of 10.
